newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FOCUS-Russia's LUKoil expands on foreign markets.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Russia's LUKoil expands on foreign markets.

text.p: Russia's largest oil company LUKoil launched a programme for foreign investors to trade preferred shares abroad and announced major plans for new international issues on Thursday.

Traders began selling American Depositary Receipts (ADRs), each representing two underlying LUKoil preferred shares, after the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission approved them late on Wednesday, the company said.

Preferred share prices of LUKoil, which accounts for about one-fifth of the Russian equity market's capitalisation, jumped to $12.60 at the close in Moscow on Thursday from $11.75 at Wednesday's close.
The head of LUKoil's securities department told Reuters the company intended to float another 15 percent of company equity on foreign markets by the end of the year to increase liquidity.

"The larger the market, the larger the circle of investors," said LUKoil Vice-President Leonid Fedun, who said the company planned to sell the government-owned stake as a special class of more prominent ADRs.

"I'm not looking for a strategic investor -- I'm looking for financial investors," Fedun said, explaining LUKoil was happy with its Western partner Atlantic Richfield Co and wanted more Russian portfolio investors -- and funds.
"We have waited four years," Fedun said of the plan to issue the 15 percent stake as level-three ADRs.
These ADRs require a company to present three years of international-standard accounts and allows companies to raise new capital.
"We think we will get the best price in 1997," he said.

Fedun said that net profits, to Russian accounting standards, which are not prepared for investment decision-making, could decline in 1997 from 1996's over 3.7 trillion roubles ($660 million), due to capital spending.
But he said oil production had risen three percent in January, year-on-year, and LUKoil still expected 1997 production to rise to 59.7 million tonnes from 58.3 million in 1996.

LUKoil also plans a level-one global depository receipt listing in London by April and has plans, which Fedun said are awaiting government approval, to issue options this year for just under five percent of shares.

The level-one preferred share ADRs introduced on Thursday, as well as level-one ADRs representing ordinary shares that are listed in Berlin, Frankfurt and on the NASDAQ bulletin board, represent existing shares of OAO Neftyanaya Kompaniya LUKoil.
"We want to make a different type of trading instrument... which offers the ability to decrease investment risk," Fedun said of the options.
LUKoil has already had talks with Japanese firms about participating in the 15 percent stake sale, he said, though he declined to give details.
By year's end, the Russian government will be left with only 6.6 percent of LUKoil, less than the 7.99 percent owned by ARCO.
After 1997, LUKoil will consider new issues of preferred shares and a Eurobond, which would bring LUKoil instruments to fixed income investors.
But Fedun said there was no need to issue a Eurobond soon.
"Only the weak (Russian) companies are trying to issue Eurobonds now, which is bad to my mind...We are not hurrying -- it will not be this year," he said.
